19K views · 8.9K reactions | Filipino food A to Z ~ O is for Okoy/Ukoy 🦐 A Filipino deep-fried fritter that is served with a vinegar dipping sauce. It is believed that it originated in the province of Laguna and comes from the Hokkien word “ō+kuè” that means “cake made from taro”. I personally like mine light & crunchy, therefore the batter is made with a cornstarch slurry. The trick to getting them crispy is to salt the veggies and remove as much water content as possible. I got this method from @Erwan @featrmedia recipe. I also prefer mine with unshelled shrimp but it’s traditionally made with smaller shrimp with the shell on. I am no pro chef, and not the best/fastest at cutting veggies so I used a mandoline! Makes 7 Ingredients: 15 shrimp, ½ chopped into bite size pieces, ½ whole 20 oz. various veggies (I used carrots, sweet potato and kalabasa squash), julienned 5 oz. bean sprouts 1 medium red onion, or 2 shallots, thinly sliced 1 bunch green onions 3 Tbsp salt 1 Tbsp fish sauce 2 tsp black or white pepper 1-2 tsp annatto powder 3/4c cold water 1.5c cornstarch Oil for frying, I used grapeseed Cilantro, for garnish (optional) Full recipe is on my website at www.krizkitch.com 🥰 #krizkitch #filipinofood #filipinorecipes #okoy #ukoy #filipino #filipinofoodatoz | krizkitch
